body.text: sāṃkhyaparibhāṣā /
body.translated_text: <s>Sāṃkhyaparibhāṣā</s> (Definitions of Sāṃkhya)

body.text:
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ /
śrīdakṣiṇāmūrtigurubhyo namaḥ /
body.translated_text:
Homage to <s>Śrī Gaṇeśa</s>.
Homage to the revered <s>Gurus</s> [beginning with] <s>Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrti</s>.

body.text: svānubhavaṃ yathāmati vyākhyāsyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: We shall expound our own experience as best we understand it.

children.text: oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya prakṛtyai puruṣāya ca /
children.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, to <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (consciousness),
To the one whose form is the essence of <s>Sāṅkhya</s> truth, the secret core of <s>Vedānta</s>.
The vision of the truth of reality is for <s>yogins</s> and supreme renunciants (<s>parahaṃsas</s>);

children.text: anyeṣāṃ ca na dātavyaṃ māyayā mohitaṃ jagat // 2 //
children.translated_text: It should not be given to others — the world is deluded by <s>Māyā</s> (illusion).

children.text: śabdaśrotā ca vyājena nirvāṇārthaṃ ca kathyate /
children.translated_text: It is taught under the pretext of word and listener for the purpose of liberation;
When some greatly fortunate one [appears], this brings rest to him.

body.text: vibhaktimatra yo paśyettasya jñānaṃ ca dūrataḥ // 3 //
body.translated_text: One who sees division here — knowledge is far from him.

children.translated_text: Now, the <s>Guru</s> (Teacher):
By the grace of the <s>Guru</s>'s method, one gains insight into the womb of the scripture.

children.text: guruśca dvividhaḥ prokto vārttikāmnāya eva ca /
children.translated_text: The <s>Guru</s> is declared to be of two kinds: the <s>Vārttika</s> (commentarial) and the <s>Āmnāya</s> (traditional lineage).
The <s>Vārttika</s> is through devotional disposition; the <s>Āmnāya</s> is the root verse-text.
However —
Those who are worshipped through the mouths of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, women, and <s>śūdras</s> are the <s>Vārttika</s> [teachers];
That which comes through the succession of <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (renunciation) etc. is proclaimed as the <s>Āmnāya</s> (traditional lineage).

children.text: ādau śivastathā viṣṇurbrahmā vasiṣṭha eva ca /
children.translated_text: First <s>Śiva</s>, then <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,

children.text: śaktaḥ pārāśaro vyāsaḥ śuko gauḍastathaiva ca //
children.translated_text: <s>Śakta</s>, <s>Pārāśara</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Śuka</s>, and <s>Gauḍa</s>,
From the venerable <s>Govindapāda</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s> — <s>Śaṅkara</s> is the supreme.
This lineage is declared as bestowing the attainment of the <s>Guru</s>'s traditional transmission.
The <s>guru</s> who gives the <s>Gāyatrī</s> initiation, the <s>guru</s> who nourishes the belly,
And the <s>Sadguru</s> (true teacher) who grants liberation — such is the threefold characteristic of a <s>guru</s>.
The study and exposition of <s>mantras</s>, ritual practices, servile arts,
Vedic craft and applied knowledge — these are attributed to that [first type of] <s>Guru</s>.
Abandoning the relation of cause and effect, <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) is the complete awakening;
He who is the liberating and salvation-granting one — he is called the <s>Sadguru</s> (true teacher).
Now, the disciple:
Holding the mind emptied of desires, with faith born of devotion to the <s>Guru</s>,
Without the aspiration for liberation there is no [true discipleship] — the <s>Guru</s> should uplift such a disciple.

children.text: bho bho svāmin kṛpāsindho prārthayiṣyāmi te 'dhunā /
children.translated_text: O Master, O ocean of compassion, I shall now entreat you:
In the forest fire of burning <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), grant liberation, O treasure of mercy!

body.text:
vidhivadadhītavedavedāṅgatvenāpātato 'rivalavedārthā asmin / tathā ca śrutiḥ -
samitpāṇiḥ śrotriyaṃ brahmaniṣṭhaṃ gurumupaśritya tamanusarati //
body.translated_text: Having duly studied the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedāṅgas</s> (limbs of the Vedas), the meanings of the <s>Vedas</s> become apparent at first glance. And thus the <s>śruti</s> (revealed scripture) says: 'With sacrificial fuel in hand, one should approach a <s>guru</s> who is learned in scripture and established in <s>Brahman</s>, and follow him.'

body.text: taddhi saṃpraṇipātena paripraśnena sevayā //
body.translated_text: Through prostration, through inquiry, and through service —

body.text: upadekṣyanti te jñānaṃ jñāninastattvadarśinaḥ // 13 //
body.translated_text: The knowers, the seers of truth, will teach you knowledge.

children.translated_text: 'Having known which, there is no further delusion' — thus in the <s>Gītā</s>.
If you desire enjoyment, dear child, abandon sense objects as if they were poison.

body.text: lolupaḥ sādhusaṅgasya atyantaṃ sukhamaśnute // 14 //
body.translated_text: One who is eager for the company of the holy attains supreme happiness.

body.text:
iti guruparamparā /
  atha sāṃkhyasāmpradāyena jñānamāha / tatra prathamaṃ sādhanacatuṣṭayasampannasya ihāmutrārthaphalabhogavirāgaḥ / dvitīyaṃ śamadamādiṣaṭkam / tṛtīyaṃ nityānityavastuvivekaḥ / caturthaṃ mumukṣatvaṃ mokṣecchā / kintu iha nāma srakcandanavanitādiviṣayabhogavirāgaḥ / amutra nāma svargabhogādianicchā / śamo nāma manonigrahaḥ / dama indriyanigrahaḥ / titikṣā śītoṣṇādiparotkarṣasahanam / samādhānaṃ sṛṣṭyādimāyāvilakṣaṇam / śraddhā gurāvadhyātmaśāstre ratiḥ / uparamaḥ kāryakāraṇātītam / nitya ātmā / anityā dṛśyapadārthāḥ / ataḥ paraṃ mokṣecchā //
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>guru-paramparā</s> (lineage of teachers). Now, knowledge is taught according to the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> tradition. Therein, first, for one endowed with the fourfold qualification (<s>sādhana-catuṣṭaya</s>): dispassion toward the fruits and enjoyments of this world and the next. Second, the sixfold [virtues] beginning with <s>śama</s> (mental tranquility) and <s>dama</s> (sense-control). Third, discrimination between the eternal and the non-eternal (<s>nitya-anitya-vastu-viveka</s>). Fourth, the desire for liberation (<s>mumukṣutva</s>), the longing for <s>mokṣa</s>. Here, 'this world' means dispassion toward sense enjoyments such as garlands, sandalwood, butter, etc. 'The next' means non-desire for heavenly enjoyments etc. <s>Śama</s> means restraint of the mind. <s>Dama</s> means restraint of the senses. <s>Titikṣā</s> (forbearance) means enduring the extremes of cold and heat etc. <s>Samādhāna</s> (concentration) means that which is distinct from the <s>māyā</s> (illusion) of creation etc. <s>Śraddhā</s> (faith) means devotion to the <s>Guru</s> and to the science of the Self. <s>Uparama</s> (cessation) means transcending cause and effect. The eternal is the <s>Ātman</s> (Self). The non-eternal are the objects of perception. Beyond this is the desire for liberation.

children.translated_text: Thus the fourfold qualification (<s>sādhana-catuṣṭaya</s>).
The blanket, the begging bowl, and the bamboo staff are the threefold marks of the intellect;
The scattered, the oscillating, and the absorbed — [these are] the three stages (<s>bhūmikā</s>).

body.text:
atha bhūmikā / vikṣeptā viṣayapadārthe ratiḥ / gatāyātā saṃśayātmikā / sulīnatā prītirūpā turīyā /
  atha buddhayaḥ / guruḥ śāstrādiyuktyā bodhayati tathāpi śūnyaṃ kambalapeśīvat / sā adhikaprakāśo na bhavati kharparacchidravat / anekayuktyā vistārayati bhagnaveṇuvat jale tailavat / tatrādau vairāgyam / tatra pramāṇaṃ śrutiḥ- na vā 're sarvasya kāmāya sarvaṃ priyaṃ bhavatyātmanastu kāmāya sarvaṃ priyaṃ bhavati iti /
  bṛhadāraṇyake 'tyāgenaikena amṛtatvamānaśuḥ'; / tatrādau śabalatyāgaḥ //
body.translated_text: Now the stages: The scattered (<s>vikṣipta</s>) is attachment to sense objects. The oscillating (<s>gatāyātā</s>) is characterized by doubt. The well-absorbed (<s>sulīnatā</s>) is of the nature of delight, the fourth [state]. Now the intellects: The <s>Guru</s> teaches through scripture and reasoning, yet [the student's mind remains] empty, like a blanket wrapped around — it does not become more illuminated, like a hole in a begging bowl. Through many reasonings [the <s>Guru</s>] expands it, like a broken bamboo, like oil in water. Therein, first is <s>vairāgya</s> (renunciation). The authority for this is the <s>śruti</s>: 'Not for the sake of everything is everything dear, but for the sake of the Self is everything dear.' In the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s>: 'Through renunciation alone they attained immortality.' Therein, first is qualified renunciation (<s>śabala-tyāga</s>).

children.text: viṣṭhāmūtraṃ ca durgandhi kṛmyagāraṃ ca naśvaram /
children.translated_text: Excrement and urine, foul-smelling, a house of worms, and perishable —
The fools who take delight in that [body's] pleasures are puffed up with 'I' and 'mine.'

children.text: kasya mātā pitā kasya kasya bhrātā sahodaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Whose is the mother, whose the father, whose the brother, whose the sibling?

children.text: kasya strī kasya putrastu narāṇāṃ karmabandhanam // 2 //
children.translated_text: Whose the wife, whose the son? For human beings, it is the bondage of <s>karma</s> (action).
Toward wife, offspring, home, fields, kinsmen, and wealth —
One should look upon all as indifferent, as if all were futile to oneself.

children.text: strīṇāṃ strīsaṅgināṃ saṅgaṃ tyaktvā dūrata ātmavān /
children.translated_text: Having abandoned the company of women and those who associate with women, far away, the self-controlled one,
Patient, dwelling in solitude, should meditate upon Me without sloth.
The tiger of the mind, entered into the forest of the body, exceedingly powerful,
Devours all people — gods, passionate, and humans.
Making the sword of knowledge firm, with <s>vairāgya</s> (renunciation) as the purification of the ground,

children.text: durlabho yasya saṃgrāmo ko 'sau śūraśca ātmavān // 6 //
children.translated_text: Rare is the battle for whom — who is that hero, that self-possessed one?
Now, pure renunciation (<s>śuddha-tyāga</s>):
The wise one, having studied the scripture, devoted to knowledge and realization,
Should abandon the scripture entirely, as one seeking grain [abandons] the chaff.
If you desire the state of <s>Brahman</s>, then listen through realized knowledge:
Dispassion toward all objects and seeing the Self in all beings.
If you desire liberation, then abandon sense objects as if they were poison;
Embrace forgiveness, straightforwardness, compassion, contentment, and truth as if they were nectar.

children.text: manasā dhyāyate yogī kṛpaṇastu dhanaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: The <s>yogin</s> meditates with the mind, just as a miser [thinks] of wealth;

children.text: manasā yena pītvā ca tena jitvā jagattrayam // 10 //
children.translated_text: Having drunk with the mind, having conquered with it, [one conquers] the three worlds.
One who moves about having abandoned all desires, free from craving,
Without possessiveness, without ego — he attains peace.
Possessing nothing, self-controlled, tranquil, of balanced mind,
He, having abandoned the marks of the stages of life, should wander beyond the reach of rules.

children.text: dehe ca śṛṇu taṃ tāta guptaprakaṭalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: In the body, hear that, dear child — the characteristics both hidden and manifest:
Ten are the hidden practices, liberation is the twelfth, [and] the natural state [is the ultimate].
The indifferent sage, tranquil, without enmity, of equal vision —
I constantly follow him and am purified by the dust of his feet.
When, O <s>Śambhu</s>, shall I become capable of uprooting <s>karma</s> (action)?
Alone, desireless, tranquil, with the hand as a bowl, sky-clad.
Abandoning all <s>dharmas</s> (duties), take refuge in Me alone;

children.text: ahaṃ tvāṃ sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ // 16 //
children.translated_text: I shall liberate you from all sins — do not grieve.

children.text: nirālambapadaṃ prāpya citte tatra layaṃ gate /
children.translated_text: Having attained the state without support, when the mind dissolves therein,

children.text: nivartante kriyāḥ sarvāḥ sa yogī nirguṇaḥ paraḥ // 17 //
children.translated_text: All activities cease — that <s>yogin</s> is beyond the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), supreme.
The bewilderment of the mind drawn by the pull of sense objects and their causes —
Just as many co-wives toss a single husband about.
Well done, well done! Hear your own interest, and from the machine of bones stay far away;
The share made by this [body] in the world creates possessiveness like that of a dog.

children.text: śṛṇu tāta dvayaṃ tyājyamāśā bhedastathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Hear, dear child, two things are to be abandoned: hope and division.
Through hope one creates wretchedness; and division only increases division.
Crying and laughing — through these one takes on the condition of a <s>piśāca</s> (ghost);

children.text: asya saṅgaṃ sadā tyajya bhava cinmātra sarvadā // 21 //
children.translated_text: Always abandoning attachment to this, be pure consciousness alone at all times.

children.text: chāyākāryaṃ yathā nāsti tathaivāyaṃ hi dehakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a shadow produces no [real] effect, so indeed is this body;
Abandoning the essence of [attachment to] household comforts, take refuge in the supreme state.
The earth is [but] a cow's hoofprint, <s>Meru</s> a post, space a ring,
The three worlds are [but] a blade of grass, O <s>Rāma</s> — such is the work adorned by <s>vairāgya</s> (renunciation).
Among thousands of human beings, scarcely one strives for perfection.

body.text: iti vairāgyam //
body.translated_text: Thus <s>vairāgya</s> (renunciation).

children.translated_text: Now, through devotion, the fourfold liberation:
One attains <s>sāyujya</s> (union), <s>sārūpya</s> (same form), and <s>sālokya</s> (same realm) with the syllables of the <s>Vedas</s>.
First, purification of the mind; second, mental worship and [external] worship;

children.text: tṛtīyaṃ ca sadā dhyānaṃ vyāpakaṃ ca caturthakam // 1 //
children.translated_text: Third, constant meditation; and the fourth is [realization of] the all-pervading.
The fifth is the supportless [state] — these are the stages of liberation in order;
A mortal who diligently practices them attains liberation — there is no doubt.
Purification of the mind is accomplished through <s>japa</s> (mantra recitation) and observance;
Afterward, the fourfold liberation — hear well, O best of the twice-born!
Through the mental [worship], attainment of the [divine] world and constant proximity to it;

children.text: tathā tasya svarūpaṃ ca nirālambena śāśvatam // 4 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, [attainment of] its very form, and through the supportless [state], the eternal.

children.text: ye ye yān yān yajandevāṃste catvāramokṣagāḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever deities whoever worships, they attain the four [types of] liberation;
Without Self-knowledge, liberation does not occur for the <s>Saccidātman</s> (Being-Consciousness-Self).

body.text:
kintu -
  mānasaṃ nāma āsanasthāṃ sāvayavamūrttiṃ dhyāyet / nivātadīpavatsvasthaṃ yathābuddhyā ṣoḍaśopacāraiḥ pūjayet / tasya gacchatastiṣṭhataśca na samīpāvabhāsaḥ / sa eva sarvabhūtasthaṃ svarūpaṃ paśyati / tataḥ sāvakāśamiva bhāsate sā sāyujyatā /
  iti caturvidhā upāsanā muktiḥ /
body.translated_text: However — the mental [worship] is as follows: one should meditate upon the embodied form with limbs, seated on a seat; steady like a lamp in a windless place, one should worship with the sixteen services (<s>ṣoḍaśopacāra</s>) as one's intellect [can conceive]; for one who goes or stands, there is no perception of proximity to it; that very one sees the essential nature dwelling in all beings; then that state of union (<s>sāyujya</s>) appears as if with space. Thus the fourfold devotional worship is liberation.

children.translated_text: Now, non-dual devotion (<s>advaita-bhakti</s>).
Devotion is seeing everything as pervaded by the Lord of all; and knowledge is the vision of non-difference.

children.text: nirapekṣaṃ ca vairāgyaṃ muktaṃ nirviṣayaṃ manaḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: Dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) is without dependence, and the mind is liberated and free from objects. // 1 //

body.text: kintu cāṇḍālādibrahmaparyantaṃ sarvabhūteṣu īśvararūpaṃ bhāvayet / yathārhaṃ ṣoḍaśopacāreṇa pūjayet / sā bhaktiḥ na tu pratimā / brahmādipipīlikāparyantaṃ svaśarīravadabhedaṃ jñātvā tajjñānaṃ paradehāhisvadehāvayamekīkṛtya sarvatra ekameva piṇḍamavadhārayet brahmādisthāvaraparyantamihāmutra nirāśā / mukti nāma vṛttiśūnyam / tatra pramāṇam -

children.translated_text: One who sees in all beings the nature of the Lord as the Self,
And [sees] beings in the Self — such a one is the best of <s>Bhāgavatas</s> (devotees of the Lord). // 2 //

body.translated_text: However, one should cultivate the vision of the Lord's form in all beings, from the <s>caṇḍāla</s> (outcaste) to <s>Brahmā</s>; one should worship with the sixteen services as appropriate. That is devotion — not [worship of] an image. Knowing non-difference — like one's own body — from <s>Brahmā</s> down to the ant, that knowledge is: making the other's body and one's own body one, one should ascertain one single mass everywhere, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to the immovable, without desire here or hereafter. Liberation (<s>mukti</s>) is devoid of mental activity. The authority for this is —

children.translated_text: When one perceives the separate existence of beings as abiding in the One,

children.text: tata eva ca vistāraṃ brahma sampadyate tadā // 3 //
children.translated_text: And from that alone their expansion — then one attains <s>Brahman</s>. // 3 //
When one completely renounces all desires that arise in the mind, O <s>Pārtha</s>,
Content in the Self by the Self alone — such a one does not grieve even in sleep. // 4 //
In the <s>Gītā</s>:
That dispassion which arises toward [everything] from <s>Brahmā</s> down to the immovable,
Just as [there is] dispassion toward crow-droppings — that is pure dispassion. // 5 //

body.text: iti advaitabhaktiḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] non-dual devotion (<s>advaita-bhakti</s>).

children.translated_text: Now, the determination of discriminative knowledge (<s>viveka-jñāna-nirṇaya</s>).
Freedom from anger, dispassion, control of the senses, forgiveness, compassion, tranquility, love of people,
Free from greed, generous — the cause of liberation from existence; these are the ten characteristics of knowledge. // 1 //
Action (<s>karma</s>), the science of the Self (<s>adhyātma-tattva</s>), and knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> beyond that,
<s>Indra</s> (the lord) — these four meanings are to be stated, having the Self as their mark, bringing happiness. // 2 //
The knower of action becomes a <s>jīva</s> (individual soul); the <s>puruṣa</s> (person) is called <s>adhyātma</s> (the inner Self);
The Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) is the knower of reality (<s>tattva</s>); 'all is <s>Brahman</s>' — that is the state of <s>Brahman</s>. // 3 //
The <s>varṇāśrama</s> (caste-and-life-stage) system and <s>dharma</s>, devotion to ritual activities such as fire-offerings,
Worship toward all beings, and knowledge — this is called <s>karma</s> (action-based knowledge). // 4 //
Dispassion, the science of the Self (<s>adhyātma-śāstra</s>), and [the state where] <s>māyā</s> (illusion) has departed,
Inquiry (<s>jijñāsā</s>), reflection (<s>manana</s>), and superimposition (<s>adhyāsa</s>) — [this] is called <s>adhyātma-jñāna</s> (Self-knowledge). // 5 //
Having examined the rules of <s>dharma</s>, <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, and other systems of <s>dharma</s>, action, and ritual procedure,
Knowledge of reality (<s>tattva-jñāna</s>) is said to be that which transcends the meaning of those. // 6 //
The meaning of the word '<s>samādhi</s>' (absorption): a mental state (<s>vṛtti</s>) in the form of <s>Brahman</s>,
Solitary, desireless, tranquil — that is called knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>. // 7 //
That from which words turn back, the mark [of <s>Brahman</s>] — all cognition having dissolved,
Shines by itself, abiding in its own nature, like the Self itself. // 8 //
For one devoid of the prescribed conduct, one's own intellect operates regarding everything;
Pursuing objects of wealth and personal gain — that <s>jīva</s> (soul) is called low. // 9 //
Ever devoted to righteous conduct, beyond dualities, and desireless,
Even eating dry [food] — such a one is called a <s>puruṣa</s> (true person). // 10 //
With only a staff and ochre robes, free from desire and anger,
Content like a bee that has eaten — such a one is called <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord). // 11 //

children.text: digvāsaṃ ca svasaṃvedyamānandaṃ svaparaṃ na hi /
children.translated_text: Clad in the directions (naked), self-knowing, blissful, neither one's own nor another's,

children.text: pāṇipātre ca yadbhuṃkte sa brahma rājate mahīm // 12 //
children.translated_text: One who eats from the hand as a bowl — that is <s>Brahman</s>, shining upon the earth. // 12 //
Always beyond the body, free from the <s>varṇāśrama</s> (caste-and-life-stage) system,
Whatever is done as righteous conduct — that one, delighting in the Self (<s>ātmārāma</s>), shines. // 13 //
Thus.
Now, in the <s>Dharma-śāstra</s> (law texts) —
The fruit of action is threefold: undesirable (<s>aniṣṭa</s>), desirable (<s>iṣṭa</s>), and mixed (<s>miśra</s>).
The animal (<s>paśu</s>), the mixed, the wise (<s>jñānī</s>), the perfected (<s>siddha</s>), and the knowable (<s>jñeya</s>) — these are five,
Endowed with [their respective] characteristics, they are described according to differences of conduct. // 14 //

children.text: uktvā uktvā ca kāryeṇa dravyaṃ ca sādhayettataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having spoken again and again, one should then accomplish wealth through action;
Devoted to the belly and genitals, seeking selfish gain — this is known as the characteristic of the animal (<s>paśu</s>). // 15 //
Those who follow the customs of the age, adhering to the approved <s>varṇa</s> (caste) and <s>āśrama</s> (life-stage),

children.text: ātmasvārthaṃ na jānāti sa miśraṃ lakṣaṇaṃ smṛtam // 16 //
children.translated_text: But do not know the self-interest of the Self — that is known as the characteristic of the mixed. // 16 //
One who knows all the meanings of the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>śāstras</s>, and who follows the prescribed conduct,

children.text: yathoktvā ca vadedvākyaṃ sa jñānī lakṣaṇocyate // 17 //
children.translated_text: And who speaks words as prescribed — such a one is called one having the characteristic of the wise (<s>jñānī</s>). // 17 //

children.text: kāryaṃ ca anyathākartuṃ yadvaktuṃ tattu sādhayet /
children.translated_text: What is to be done and how to do it otherwise, what is to be said and how to accomplish it,
The wise one who speaks of accumulated wealth — that is called the characteristic of perfection (<s>siddhi</s>). // 18 //
Abandoning the agency of cause and effect, one should wander the earth,
Beyond even praise, desireless — bliss is the characteristic of the knowable (<s>jñeya</s>). // 19 //
Thus [ends] the determination of discriminative knowledge (<s>viveka-jñāna-nirṇaya</s>).
<s>Dharmas</s> (duties) depend on the body and <s>varṇa</s> (caste), fabricated by the imaginations of the <s>Vedas</s>;
They should be discarded like a snake's slough — 'I am that One, the stainless (<s>nirañjana</s>).' // 20 //
Therefore, from the <s>Śruti</s> (scripture): 'Liberation (<s>kaivalya</s>) is through knowledge'; and from the <s>Gītā</s>: 'Whose actions are burned by the fire of knowledge.'
Indirect (<s>parokṣa</s>) is scriptural knowledge; direct (<s>aparokṣa</s>) is the eternal;
The first [concerns] birth and actions; the second is of the nature of Being-Consciousness (<s>sat-cit</s>). // 21 //
That which has creation, sustenance, and dissolution is united with beings;

children.text: ātmā ca tatra sākṣī ca jagaddraṣṭā ca sūryavat // 22 //
children.translated_text: The Self (<s>Ātman</s>) is the witness therein, and the seer of the world, like the sun. // 22 //
The manifest form of the elements, both the unmoving and the moving —
One should see that like a magic show; the world is like waves. // 23 //
A being bound by imagination always prattles like one afflicted;
The body dances in the streets until it falls to the ground. // 24 //
People exhibit the behavior of children possessed by demons — what shame is there for the assemblies of <s>yogīs</s>?
They utter various words — for what purpose, regarding happiness and sorrow? // 25 //

children.text: asti bhāti priyaṃ sthiramasthiraṃ nāma rūpakam /
children.translated_text: Existence (<s>asti</s>), luminosity (<s>bhāti</s>), and dearness (<s>priya</s>) are permanent; name (<s>nāma</s>) and form (<s>rūpa</s>) are impermanent.
The four desires (<s>eṣaṇā</s>) should be renounced — 'I am that One, the stainless (<s>nirañjana</s>).' // 26 //
The form of <s>mātṛkā</s> (alphabet) and sound operates through the cosmic <s>māyā</s> (illusion);
Know that sound therein — the meaning [grasped through words] is futile. // 27 //

children.text: amanastu sadā deho yathā grāmo vinā janāt /
children.translated_text: A body without a mind is like a village without people;
Even <s>Brahmā</s> should not be made responsible — such a one is an animal (<s>paśu</s>), a self-destroyer. // 28 //
The highest [form of worship] is absorption in dissolution (<s>laya</s>); <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) are the middle;
Image-worship (<s>pratimā-pūjā</s>) is the lowest; singing and dancing is the lowest of the low. // 29 //
Bathing is [purification of] the mind — renouncing impurity; purity (<s>śauca</s>) is restraint of the senses;
Knowledge is seeing non-difference; meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) is a mind free from objects. // 30 //

children.text: sthūlapeśivat pratyakṣaṃ liṅgaṃ vandhyaṃ yathā striyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The gross [body] is perceptible like flesh; the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) is like a barren woman;
Through the mind, in the form of oneness with the Self — that itself is <s>Brahman</s>, eternal. // 31 //
Full of the meaning of <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) and <s>Smṛti</s> (tradition), with the fragrance of the mind in <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) —
So long as there is identification with the body, all actions are fruitless. // 32 //
One attached to worldly actions who thinks 'I am <s>Brahman</s>'
Is fallen from both action and <s>Brahman</s> — one should abandon such a person like an outcast. // 33 //
Distraction from <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) takes many forms of reasoning;
Until the body perishes, these do not cease causing delusion. // 34 //

children.text: ekosau yogavāsī ca dvayaṃ grāmastathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: One alone is a <s>yoga</s>-dweller; two constitutes a village;
Three is a city — so I regard [the life] of forest-dwellers. // 35 //
The <s>Vedas</s>, <s>śāstras</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and various reasonings eloquently [presented] —
True intellect is of the nature of resolve (<s>vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ</s>), not of the form of [mere] practice. // 36 //
Having churned the four <s>Vedas</s> and all the <s>śāstras</s> continually,

children.text: yo vai tattvaṃ na jānāti darvīpākarasaṃ yathā // 37 //
children.translated_text: One who does not know the reality is like a ladle [that stirs] the cooking but [does not taste] the flavor. // 37 //
If one proficient in the word-<s>Brahman</s> (<s>śabda-brahman</s>) would bathe in the Supreme —
His effort and its fruit are like a guardian of a barren cow. // 38 //
In the mirror of space, in which this entire world is reflected,
All that is of the form of <s>Brahman</s>, and [yet] the sport of <s>māyā</s> (illusion). // 39 //

children.text: yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī /
children.translated_text: That which is night for all beings — in that the self-controlled one is awake;

children.text: yasyāṃ jāgarti bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ // 40 //
children.translated_text: That in which beings are awake is night for the seeing sage. // 40 //

children.text: nāhaṃ deho na ca prāṇo nendriyāṇi tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: I am not the body, nor the vital breath (<s>prāṇa</s>), nor indeed the senses,

children.text: na mano hanta buddhiśca naiva cittamahaṅkṛtiḥ // 41 //
children.translated_text: Nor the mind (<s>manas</s>), nor indeed the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), nor consciousness (<s>citta</s>), nor the ego (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>). // 41 //

children.text: nāhaṃ manuṣyo na ca deva yakṣo na brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyavaiśyaśūdraḥ /
children.translated_text: I am not a human, nor a <s>deva</s> (god), nor a <s>yakṣa</s> (nature spirit); not a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>kṣatriya</s>, <s>vaiśya</s>, or <s>śūdra</s>;

children.text: na brahmacārī na gṛhī vanastho bhikṣurna cāhaṃ nijabodharūpaḥ // 42 //
children.translated_text: Not a celibate student (<s>brahmacārī</s>), not a householder (<s>gṛhī</s>), not a forest-dweller (<s>vanastha</s>), not a mendicant (<s>bhikṣu</s>) — I am of the nature of my own awareness (<s>nijabodha</s>). // 42 //
The activity of cause and effect — threefold, created by imagination,
Conjoined with mind and ego — is futile, a mere garland of words. // 43 //

children.text: śabde śabdasya jñānārthaṃ yogī vadati nispṛhaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>yogī</s>, desireless, speaks in words for the purpose of conveying knowledge through words,
Just as sound in musical instruments operates dependently. // 44 //
The <s>yogī</s> performs all activities in the course of bodily action;

children.text: kaumāraṃ krīḍanaṃ caiva sarvaṃ mithyaiva kāraṇam // 45 //
children.translated_text: Childhood play and all [such things] are merely illusory causes. // 45 //
Whatever and however a being acts, a person shines in his own home;

children.text: yo yo yasya yathā bhāvastattateṣāṃ ca saukhyatā // 46 //
children.translated_text: Whatever is the disposition of whoever — therein lies their happiness. // 46 //
All that striving for desires is futile in the long run.

children.text: na cāsya kriyā kācinneha nānāsti karhicit // 47 //
children.translated_text: And there is no action whatsoever belonging to it; here there is never any multiplicity. (47)

children.text: ahaṃ ceṣṭa ito dehe sarvakarmasu ceṣṭate /
children.translated_text: 'I act' — thus in this body it engages in all actions;
One should know that knowledge by which, through remembrance, [true] knowledge arises. (48)

children.text: taḍāgaḥ pūrṇato yena yaddātuṃ balaṃ rājate /
children.translated_text: Just as a reservoir, when full, has the power to give water,
So through a small opening, the primary activities of the mind and self [flow forth] like water. (49)
Having abandoned bondage, let them make the mind complete and tranquil;

children.text: ye hi yuktiṃ sadābhyāsātsa vai jñānottamottamaḥ // 50 //
children.translated_text: One who is ever united through constant practice — that person is the highest of the highest in knowledge. (50)
All actions of the body and so forth — you are known in both knowledge and ignorance;
'I am that' — in the form of pure consciousness alone — know this as the mark of <s>Brahman</s>. (51)

children.text: ahaṃ mūrkhamahaṃ jñātā yo dharmaḥ pratipādyate /
children.translated_text: 'I am a fool, I am a knower' — whatever <s>dharma</s> is taught,
'I am that' — in the form of pure consciousness alone — know this as the mark of <s>Brahman</s>. (52)
The knot of the heart is pierced; all doubts are cut asunder;

children.text: kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi yasmin dṛṣṭe parāvare // 53 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>karmas</s> of that person are exhausted — in whom the supreme and the inferior are seen. (53)
The world is distinct from <s>Brahman</s>; there is nothing whatsoever other than <s>Brahman</s>;
Upon <s>Brahman</s>, the illusory consciousness appears — just like a desert mirage. (54)
For the <s>yogin</s> who is satisfied with the nectar of knowledge and has accomplished all that is to be done,

children.text: na cāsti kiñcitkartavyamasti cenna sa sattvavit // 55 //
children.translated_text: There is nothing more to be done; if there is, then he is not a knower of reality. (55)

children.text: na tvaṃ viprādiko varṇo nāśramī nākṣagocaraḥ /
children.translated_text: You are not a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> or any other <s>varṇa</s> (caste); you are not an <s>āśramin</s> (member of a life-stage); you are not an object of the senses;
You are unattached, formless, the witness of the universe — be happy! (56)
When the identification with the body has dissolved, and the Self of consciousness is realized,

children.text: yatra yatra mano yāti tatra tatra samādhayaḥ // 57 //
children.translated_text: Wherever the mind goes, there and there alone is <s>samādhi</s>. (57)
For one established in the sole reality of the Self, whatever actions one performs — that is worship;

children.text: yo yo jalpaḥ sa saṃmantrastaddhyānaṃ ca nirīkṣaṇam // 58 //
children.translated_text: Whatever speech one utters — that is <s>mantra</s>; and contemplation upon that is meditation. (58)
Neither conceptual thought nor its absence, nor latent impressions of dissolved limiting adjuncts —
Immersed in one's own true nature, that <s>yogin</s> is a knower of the supreme reality. (59)
All the senses beginning with the body function by mere existence alone,

children.text: yathā dīpe prapaṃcasya cuṃbakaṃ lohameva ca // 60 //
children.translated_text: Just as [objects are seen] by the light of a lamp, and iron [moves] by the presence of a magnet. (60)

children.text: dehadvayaṃ tathā nāma varṇāśramā ca vyarthatā /
children.translated_text: Likewise, the two bodies, names, <s>varṇas</s> (castes), and <s>āśramas</s> (life-stages) become purposeless;
'Earth, space, <s>Brahman</s>, I' — this suffices through <s>samādhi</s>. (61)
How can there be meditation on the unmanifest? How can the all-pervading be dismissed?

children.text: amūrtasya kathaṃ pūjā svayaṃ brahma sanātanam // 62 //
children.translated_text: How can there be worship of the formless? [For] one is oneself the eternal <s>Brahman</s>. (62)

children.text: phalasya kāraṇaṃ puṣpaṃ phale puṣpaṃ vinaśyati /
children.translated_text: The flower is the cause of the fruit; when the fruit appears, the flower perishes;

children.text: jñānasya kāraṇaṃ karma jñāne karma vinaśyati // 63 //
children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> (action) is the cause of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge); when knowledge arises, <s>karma</s> perishes. (63)

children.text: kiṃ karomi kva gacchāmi kiṃ gṛhṇāmi tyajāmi kim /
children.translated_text: What shall I do? Where shall I go? What shall I take? What shall I renounce?
Everything is filled by the Self, just as [everything is filled] by the waters of the great cosmic dissolution. (64)
The manifest form beginning with the elements, and both the moving and the unmoving —
One should see the world as like a magic show, like waves upon water. (65)
Having divided a word into two parts, it is useless for the one united with knowledge and meaning;

children.text: kadācidvaktuṃ jñānārthaṃ vyartho vaktuṃ na śakyate // 66 //
children.translated_text: Sometimes to speak the meaning of knowledge — the useless cannot be spoken. (66)

children.text: garvaṃ no vahate na nindanti parānno bhāṣate niṣṭhuraṃ
children.translated_text: One bears no pride, does not criticize others, does not speak harshly,

children.text: proktaṃ kenacidapriyaṃ ca hasate krodhaṃ ca nālambate /
children.translated_text: Laughs at disagreeable words spoken by anyone and does not resort to anger;
Having heard a faulty composition made by another, one remains as if mute —

children.text: ddoṣānnādadate svayaṃ na kurute caitatsatāṃ lakṣaṇam // 67 //
children.translated_text: One does not take in faults nor commits them oneself — this is the mark of the virtuous. (67)

children.text: bījamadhye yathā vṛkṣaṃ vṛkṣamadhye ca bījatā /
children.translated_text: Just as a tree exists within a seed, and the seed-nature within a tree,
The all-pervading Self, pervaded and pervader, is not seen as separate. (68)
If the Self is one in all beings, how can bondage and liberation be twofold?
Through the force of birth and <s>saṃskāras</s> (impressions), differentiation always persists. (69)
Just as a reflection [varies] according to its limiting adjunct — long, oblique, or circular —
Therefore, how can the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), being of different characteristics, become one? (70)
According to birth, conduct, and in conformity with prior <s>karma</s>,
According to the qualification for that particular knowledge — there are two kinds, of bondage and of liberation. (71)
Just as the faultless arising of <s>prārabdha</s> (commenced karma) takes manifold forms,
So too pleasure and pain — how can there be oneness? (72)

children.text: dravyaṃ na bhakṣayetprājñaḥ svadravyaṃ naiva poṣayet /
children.translated_text: The wise person should not consume [another's] substance, nor should one nourish one's own substance [excessively];

children.text: santuṣṭaḥ sarvadā nityaṃ sa naro jñānavānbhavet // 73 //
children.translated_text: One who is always and perpetually content — that person becomes a knower. (73)

children.text: śarīraṃ naśvaraṃ sarvaṃ sambandhaḥ kintu śāśvataḥ /
children.translated_text: The body is entirely perishable, but the connection [with the Self] is eternal;
By means of age and the thread of [life's] path, it goes to its respective stations. (74)

children.text: yathā paragṛhe vāso mārgasthaṃ kurute sadā /
children.translated_text: Just as dwelling in another's house always makes one feel like a traveler on the road,

children.text: tathaiva sukhaduḥkhena na spṛśet jñānino naraḥ // 75 //
children.translated_text: So too, the man of knowledge is not touched by pleasure and pain. (75)

children.text: naṭī ca naṭanāṭyaṃ ca nānākrīḍā ca rañjanam /
children.translated_text: An actress, her acting and dance, various plays and entertainments —

children.text: ahaṃ pratyayajānāti tathaiva jño sadā naraḥ // 76 //
children.translated_text: The 'I'-notion knows [these]; so too, the knowing person always [witnesses]. (76)

body.text: iti jñānanirṇayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the determination of knowledge (<s>jñānanirṇaya</s>).

body.text:
atha śrotā uvāca /
idaṃ kiṃ dṛśyate kena kathaṃ jātam ?
taṃ hovāca-
prathama anādivastu caitanya ātmā / tasya sphuraṇaṃ jātaṃ sa imamevātmānaṃ dvidhā pātayettataḥ /
patiśca patnī cābhavatāmiti bṛhadāraṇye /
tattvamasīti yasmin tripadāni bhavanti / tat tvaṃ asi / brahmāhamasmīti sakalabrahmāntaṃ niśvasitam / atha tatsarvaṃ tvameva / idamāścaryam / tarhi citta ekāgram atisūkṣmataraṃ kuru / paramarthamityuktam / ātmā 'yaṃ gururacaladharmavyāpakatvāditi / atha-

children.translated_text: The blind and the lame are in association, and from that association action is established;
Where the lame one has independence, there the blind one becomes fruitless. (1)

body.translated_text: Then the listener said: 'What is this that is seen? By whom? How was it born?' To that, [the teacher] replied: First, the beginningless reality — consciousness, the Self. Its manifestation arose; it divided itself into two. 'There became a husband and a wife' — thus [it is stated] in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> [Upaniṣad]. '<s>Tat tvam asi</s>' (That thou art) — in which the three words occur: <s>tat</s>, <s>tvam</s>, <s>asi</s>. '<s>Brahma aham asmi</s>' (I am <s>Brahman</s>) — up to the entirety of <s>Brahman</s>...

children.translated_text: That which transcends the blind one is the lame one — immovable and eternal;
It exists both externally and internally, and is seen like space. (2)

body.text:
kintu māyā andhā avivekitvāt / ubhayorekībhūtvā mithyā jīveśvarau vyājenāpi brahmāṇḍayoḥ / sṛṣṭinirmitāḥ /
tasmānmāyāparityāgena svayameva cidākāśe ca vartate /
tatra pramāṇaṃ śrutiḥ / ākāśa ātmā khaṃ brahma /
  atha jīveśvarayorlakṣaṇam / tatra pramāṇaṃ śrutiḥ / dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāyā samānaṃ vṛkṣaṃ pariṣasvajāte / tayoranyaḥ pippalaṃ svādvattyanaśnannanyo abhicākaśīti / atha vedeti / kāryopādicaitanyaṃ jīvaśabdavācyam / kāraṇopādhicaitanyam īśvaraśabdavācyam /

children.translated_text: The <s>jīva</s> has the effect (<s>kārya</s>) as its limiting adjunct; <s>Īśvara</s> has the cause (<s>kāraṇa</s>) as its limiting adjunct;
Having abandoned the relation of cause and effect, full awakening is established. (3)

body.translated_text: However, <s>Māyā</s> is blind due to lack of discrimination. The two, having become unified, falsely [produce] <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) and <s>Īśvara</s> (Lord) — even through artifice, in both the microcosm and macrocosm. Creation is produced [by them]. Therefore, by abandoning <s>Māyā</s>, one abides in the space of consciousness (<s>cidākāśa</s>) by oneself. The authority for this is <s>Śruti</s>: 'Space is the Self; the void is <s>Brahman</s>.' Now, the definition of <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>. The authority is <s>Śruti</s>: 'Two birds, companions, cling to the same tree...'

body.text: tatra kāryaṃ nāma ahaṅkārādisṛṣṭivyāpāraḥ kāraṇaṃ nāma sākṣī hyantaḥsphuraṇam / iti vedānte /

children.translated_text: The overseer, the permitter, the supporter, the enjoyer, the great Lord —
He is also called the supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) — the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> in this body. (4)

body.translated_text: There, the 'effect' means the operation of creation beginning with <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego); the 'cause' means the witness — the inner illumination. Thus [it is stated] in <s>Vedānta</s>.

children.translated_text: Thus [is described] <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord).

children.text: puruṣaḥ prakṛtistho hi bhuṅkte prakṛtijān guṇān /
children.translated_text: The <s>Puruṣa</s>, situated in <s>Prakṛti</s>, experiences the <s>guṇas</s> born of <s>Prakṛti</s>;
The cause of his birth in good and evil wombs is his association with the <s>guṇas</s>. (1)
Thus [is described] the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul).
The reflection of the face seen in a mirror —

children.text: mukhatvāpṛthak te na hi vā 'sti vastu //
children.translated_text: It is not separate from the face, nor is it a [real] thing;

body.text: cidābhāsako 'dhīśajīvo 'pi tadvat

children.translated_text: That Self, whose nature is eternal apprehension, am I. (1)

body.translated_text: The reflection of consciousness as the <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> is likewise —

body.text:
iti hastāmale / salila eko iṣṭādvaito bhavati / iti bṛhadāraṇye / tathā bimbapratibimbanyāyena jīveśvarau kalpitau / tajjīvasya mokṣasādhanamāha karmaparaṃ aharahaḥ sandhyāmupāsitā yāvajjīvamagnihotraṃ juhuyāt / jyotiṣṭomau svargakāmo yajet / oṃmiti brahma / omitīdaoṃ sarvam / omityagnihotramanujānāti /
  iti karma /
atha jñānaparam / na karmaṇā na prajayā dhanena tyāgenaike amṛtatvamānaśuḥ /
prathamamāyāśabalasṛṣṭyādiputrakalatradravyādvilakṣaṇaḥ / dvitīyaṃ sthūlasūkṣmādiśarīrasya vilakṣaṇam / tṛtīyaṃ kevalamokṣasaṅkalpaḥ / yathā śukanālakānyāyena mithyārajjusarppe bhramamāṇe sati tasya mokṣasādhanamāha / tatra jīvasvarūpaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ dṛṣṭisambandhena sūryaprabhayā pratibhāti tadvāsanā mahad hṛdi granthiḥ /

children.translated_text: Thus ends the definition of the <s>jīva</s>.

children.text: jīvasya mokṣakāmāya trivargaṃ ca purā kṛtam /
children.translated_text: For the <s>jīva</s> desiring liberation, the triple group [of paths] was formerly established;
<s>Karma</s> (action), <s>Pātañjala</s> (Yoga), and <s>Sāṃkhya</s> — these are described in summary. (1)

body.translated_text: Thus [it is stated] in the <s>Hastāmalaka</s>. 'In water, the one [Self] becomes the beloved non-dual' — thus in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s>. Likewise, by the analogy of object and reflection, <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> are constructed. For the liberation of that <s>jīva</s>, the means of liberation is stated: action is primary — one should worship the <s>Sandhyā</s> daily; one should offer <s>Agnihotra</s> as long as one lives; one desiring heaven should perform the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> sacrifice. '<s>Oṃ</s>' is <s>Brahman</s>; '<s>Oṃ</s>' is all this; '<s>Oṃ</s>' — one should perform the <s>Agnihotra</s>...

children.translated_text: Worship consisting of the five elements is the prescribed method — hear this in summary;

children.text: trayaṃ karma pūjāyogyaṃ vā yo pātañjale smṛtaḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: The threefold <s>karma</s> suitable for worship is what is remembered in the <s>Pātañjala</s> [system]. (2)

children.text: dvayaṃ dehābhimānena ekaṃ nāhaṃ ca sāṃkhyatā /
children.translated_text: The twofold [path consists in] identification with the body; the single [path] of 'I am not [the body]' constitutes <s>Sāṃkhya</s>;

children.text: ahaṃ nāhaṃ dvayaṃ śabdabandhamokṣaṃ ca kārakam // 3 //
children.translated_text: 'I' and 'not-I' — this pair of words constitutes the bondage and liberation, and their agency. (3)

body.text: tathā ca śrutiḥ / athāto dharmajijñāsā / athāto brahmajijñāsā / pūrvapūrvaśrutiyuktyānubhavābhāsānāmuttarottaraśrutiyuktānubhavābhāsabodhadarśanāt /

children.translated_text: The general <s>śāstra</s> is subordinate; the specific one is more authoritative.
Or let the refutation of the previous [view] by the later be mostly seen herein. [verse 4]

body.translated_text: And thus the <s>Śruti</s> [says]: 'Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>dharma</s>'; 'Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>.' Because the earlier appearances of <s>Śruti</s>, reasoning, and experience are superseded by the later <s>Śruti</s>, reasoning, and experience in their illuminating understanding —

body.text:
iti vedānte karmaparam / jñānādeva tu kaivalyamityādiśruteḥ /
na hi jñānena sadṛśaṃ pavitramiha vidyate /
jñānāgnidagdhakarmāṇi /
udarāḥ sarva evaite jñānī tvātmaiva me matam /
  iti jñānaparam /
body.translated_text: Thus in <s>Vedānta</s>, what pertains to <s>karma</s> (action). But from the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) that says 'Through knowledge alone comes <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation)' and so forth — 'There is nothing as purifying as knowledge in this world'; 'Those whose <s>karmas</s> are burned by the fire of knowledge'; 'All these are indeed noble, but the <s>jñānin</s> (knower) is my very Self — this is my view' — thus what pertains to knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>).

children.translated_text: Now, the <s>karma-yoga</s> (discipline of action) as taught in the <s>Vedas</s>:
The <s>dharma</s> (duty) of <s>varṇa</s> (social class) and <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life), preceded by the injunctions of the <s>Vedas</s> and so forth —
that is either accomplishable or not accomplishable, and it yields the fruits of birth and action. [verse 1]
In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> [sacrifice], creation would occur; the listener would be involved in the ritual —
Negated by prohibitions and injunctions, it does not become the means to liberation. [verse 2]
Through the gateway of <s>japa</s> (mantra recitation) and observances (<s>anuṣṭhāna</s>), the grace of the deity would arise;
From that [deity], <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) would come, free from the limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) of consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>). [verse 3]

body.text: tatra bhūtapūjā / pārthivasthāvarāditīrthayātrā agnihotrajvālāmukhīyāgādi / āpaḥ gaṅgāyāḥ naimiṣāraṇyādijalapūjā / tathā ca-

children.translated_text: <s>Saṃhitā</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Āraṇyaka</s>, the initiation of dualities (<s>dvandva-dīkṣā</s>), <s>Nighaṇṭaka</s> (glossary),

children.text: jyotiṣaṃ ca niruktaṃ ca daśagranthāni sūtrakam // 4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Jyotiṣa</s> (astronomy) and <s>Nirukta</s> (etymology) — ten texts, and the <s>Sūtra</s>. [verse 4]

body.translated_text: Therein, worship of the elements (<s>bhūta-pūjā</s>): pilgrimage to sacred sites of earthly and stationary [objects]; <s>Agnihotra</s> (fire offering), <s>Jvālāmukhī</s> sacrifices and the like; waters: worship of waters such as the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Naimiṣāraṇya</s>, and so forth. And likewise —

children.text: ekayā liṅgagranthyā ca baddhyate sakalaṃ jagat /
children.translated_text: By a single knot of the <s>liṅga</s> (mark), the entire world is bound;

children.text: daśagranthyā yadā baddho tasya muktiḥ kathaṃ bhavet // 5 //
children.translated_text: When one is bound by ten knots, how can liberation be for that person? [verse 5]
Thus one who recites [merely] the egoistic syllables of the <s>Vedas</s> [does so only for] bodily sustenance;

children.text: etejjñānaparaṃ jñātvā sa mukto nātra saṃśayaḥ // 6 //
children.translated_text: One who knows this supreme knowledge beyond [mere recitation] — he is liberated, there is no doubt herein. [verse 6]
However —
<s>Saṃhitā</s> [truly means] the meter of the effect, and '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' [means] 'the visible is <s>Brahman</s>';
Taking refuge in space as the '<s>Āraṇyaka</s>' (forest text), the meter is the statement 'I am <s>Brahman</s>.' [verse 7]
'<s>Śikṣā</s>' (phonetics) is the restraint of the mind from the beginning; '<s>Nighaṇṭa</s>' is the holding of [mental] activity;
'<s>Jyotiṣa</s>' (astronomy) is discrimination (<s>viveka</s>), and this '<s>Sūtra</s>' of mine is said to be the Sun. [verse 8]
'<s>Nirukta</s>' (etymology) is the cutting of doubt; '<s>Sūtra</s>-recitation' is the vision of knowledge;

children.text: annopādhiśca vedādyā yastaṃ veda sa vedavit // 9 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Vedas</s> and so forth are [merely] limiting adjuncts of food (<s>anna</s>) — one who knows that is a knower of the <s>Veda</s>. [verse 9]

body.text:
asyārthaḥ / saṃhitā nāma svahitam / kāryakāraṇātītaṃ na tu karmacodanā / brāhmaṇaṃ nāma sarvasvaṃ brahmaiva na tu yāgādi / āraṇyaṃ nāma nabhalakṣyaṃ na tu āraṇyarodanam / chando nāma brahmāsmīti smaraṇaṃ na tu piśācavacchalanam / śikṣā nāma śāsanaṃ mana ādidhāraṇā na tu pāṭhaḥ nighaṇṭaṃ nāma kāṭhinyaṃ vṛttisāvadhanatā na tu deśāntaram / jyotiṣaṃ nāma vivekata na tu gaṇakādivyāpāraḥ / sūtraṃ nāma abhedānusandhānaṃ na tu karmapreraṇā / niruktaṃ nāma saṃśayacchedyaṃ na tu vedārthaprauḍhiḥ / sūtrapāṭhaṃ nāma jñānadṛṣṭiḥ / na tu vyākaraṇabalam /
  etajjñānaṃ paraṃ jñānamanyatsaṃsārapoṣaṇam /
iti vedoktakarmayogaḥ / pramāṇaṃ vedākṣarāṇāṃ sāyujyaṃ sarūpatāṃ salokatāmaśnuta iti śruteḥ //
body.translated_text: The meaning of this is: '<s>Saṃhitā</s>' means 'one's own well-being' (<s>svahita</s>), beyond cause and effect, not an injunction to ritual action. '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' means 'everything is <s>Brahman</s> itself,' not sacrifice and the like. '<s>Āraṇyaka</s>' means 'having space as its aim,' not weeping in the forest. '<s>Chandas</s>' (meter) means the remembrance 'I am <s>Brahman</s>,' not deception like that of a <s>piśāca</s> (ghost). '<s>Śikṣā</s>' (phonetics) means instruction, the holding of the mind from the beginning, not [mere] recitation. '<s>Nighaṇṭa</s>' (glossary) means firmness, attentiveness of mental activity, not [knowledge of] other regions. '<s>Jyotiṣa</s>' (astronomy) means discrimination, not the occupation of astrologers and the like. '<s>Sūtra</s>' means the investigation of non-difference, not the prompting of ritual action. '<s>Nirukta</s>' (etymology) means the cutting of doubt, not the elaboration of Vedic meaning. '<s>Sūtra</s>-recitation' means the vision of knowledge, not the power of grammar. 'This knowledge is the supreme knowledge; everything else nourishes <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence).' Thus the <s>karma-yoga</s> as taught in the <s>Vedas</s>. The proof: from the <s>śruti</s> that says 'One attains <s>sāyujya</s> (union), <s>sārūpya</s> (same form), and <s>sālokya</s> (same realm) with the syllables of the <s>Vedas</s>.'

children.translated_text: Now, the <s>Pātañjala</s>-<s>Haṭha Yoga</s>:
Now he explains the <s>Pātañjala Yoga</s>, its limbs in order:
Liberation is to be accomplished through the body; hear the knowledge that is its means. [verse 1]

body.text: tatra haṃsopaniṣadi- gudamavaṣṭabhyādhārādvāyumutthāpya svādhiṣṭhānaṃ triḥpradakṣiṇīkṛtya maṇipūrakaṃ gatvā anāhatamatikramya viśuddhe prāṇānniruddhya ājñāmanu brahmarandhraṃ dhyāyet / tatra nādamanubhavati ciṇiti prathamaḥ 1 ciṇiciṇi 2 ghaṇṭā 3 śaṅkha 4 tantrī 5 tāla 6 veṇu 7 bheri 8 mṛdaṅga 9 megha 10 navamaṃ tyājyaṃ daśamamabhyaset / tasmānmano vilīnaṃ bhavati / yasya manasi viṣṭanā manaso 'ntarāyaṃ mano na veda yasya manaḥ śarīraṃ yo manontaro yamayati /

children.text: cakraṃ sapta trikūṭaṃ ca śrīhaṭhaṃ gohaṭhaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: The seven <s>cakras</s>, <s>Trikūṭa</s>, <s>Śrīhaṭha</s>, <s>Gohaṭha</s>,
The knot between the eyebrows (<s>bhrūvorgumphā</s>), <s>Brahmarandhra</s>, the trident (<s>sūla</s>), the vehicle (<s>yāna</s>), <s>Jālandhara</s>; [verse 1]

body.translated_text: Therein, in the <s>Haṃsopaniṣad</s>: Having pressed against the rectum, raising the breath (<s>vāyu</s>) from the <s>Ādhāra</s> (base), circumambulating the <s>Svādhiṣṭhāna</s> three times, going to the <s>Maṇipūraka</s>, passing beyond the <s>Anāhata</s>, restraining the <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths) at the <s>Viśuddhi</s>, one should meditate following the <s>Ājñā</s> on the <s>Brahmarandhra</s> (aperture of <s>Brahman</s>). There one experiences the <s>nāda</s> (inner sound): '<s>ciṇi</s>' is the first (1), '<s>ciṇiciṇi</s>' (2), bell (3), conch (4), stringed instrument (5), cymbal (6), flute (7), drum (8), <s>mṛdaṅga</s> (9), thunder (10). The ninth should be abandoned; the tenth should be practiced. Thereby the mind becomes dissolved. For one in whose mind there is penetration, there is no obstacle of the mind; the mind does not know [itself]; [it is] one whose mind is the body, who inwardly controls the mind.

children.text: ṭālī lolī tathā dhotī lambikāśodhanaṃ kramāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Ṭālī</s>, <s>Lolī</s>, also <s>Dhotī</s>, purification of the <s>Lambikā</s> in order,

children.text: khecarī bhūcarī caiva mahākāṣṭhā tathaiva ca // 2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Khecarī</s>, <s>Bhūcarī</s>, and also <s>Mahākāṣṭhā</s>; [verse 2]
<s>Udgāna</s> (ascent), <s>Lopana</s> (disappearance), <s>Gāṭhana</s> (binding), and <s>Avakāśa</s> (space),
<s>Iḍā</s> and <s>Piṅgalā</s> — [these are] twenty-eight names in sequence. [verse 3]

children.text: praṇavaṃ vyāharan jāpyaṃ so 'haṃ yāmaṃ matāntare /
children.translated_text: Reciting the <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ) as <s>jāpya</s> (mantra to be recited), '<s>so'ham</s>' (I am That) [recited] at each <s>yāma</s> (watch), according to another view;
The doer of this is the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), in conformity with the body-vessel;
Through practice (<s>sādhana</s>), <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) arises; I grow and am born. [verse 4]
<s>Aṇimā</s> (minuteness) and the other [powers] would come to those; past, future, and present;
Perfection of speech, the deceased's liberation — these are honored through association with the body. [verse 5]

children.text: yathā prete kṣamā liṅgaṃ tatsakāśācca saukhyatā /
children.translated_text: Just as in the dead [body], the <s>liṅga</s> (mark/subtle body) has the capacity, and from that comes happiness,
So through the wind of the body, the sense of 'I' and 'mine' is honored. [verse 6]

children.text: brahmarandhre gate prāṇe hyahaṃ mokṣo 'pi jāyate /
children.translated_text: When <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) enters the <s>Brahmarandhra</s>, indeed the liberation of 'I' also arises;
Just as a householder fleeing from a burning house — [such] happiness is honored. [verse 7]
Again, the ego-based dwelling — <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) gives birth;
Thus liberation while in the body is intelligence of the childish sort. [verse 8]

body.text: tatra gītā-

children.translated_text: Just as a person, having cast off worn-out garments,
takes other new ones,
so the embodied one, having cast off worn-out bodies,
enters into other new ones. [verse 9]

body.translated_text: Therein, from the <s>Gītā</s>:

body.text: draṣṭā dṛśyaṃ yadā vartte dehe saṅgena mokṣakaḥ (?) /

children.translated_text: How can the <s>Ātman</s>, the embodied one, be [limited] — being all-pervading and of distinctive nature? [verse 10]

body.translated_text: When the seer and the seen operate, liberation through association with the body [is claimed];

children.translated_text: Therefore the <s>yogin</s> who opens [the eye of knowledge], though deficient in <s>Kaula</s> (tantric) instruction,
<s>Samādhi</s> (absorption) and other [practices] are futile through association with the body. [verse 11]
The <s>Ātman</s> is consciousness (<s>prajñāna</s>), bliss (<s>ānanda</s>), eternally pure, and free from affliction;
One should move about through cognition alone, always transcending the body. [verse 12]
As long as there is identification with the body, and as long as <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) operates,
So long does the giving of birth-knowledge occur, in accordance with <s>karma</s> (action). [verse 13]

body.text: tatra niṣedhārthaśrutiḥ-

children.translated_text: Not through action, not through progeny, not through wealth —
Through renunciation alone did some attain immortality.
That [<s>Brahman</s>], beyond heaven, hidden in the cave [of the heart],
Shines forth, which the ascetics enter.

body.translated_text: Therein, the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) with the purpose of prohibition:

body.text: vedāntavijñānasuniścitārthāḥ saṃnyāsayogādyatayaḥ śuddhasattvāḥ iti śruteḥ / ābrahmabhuvanāllokāt iti gītāsu /

children.translated_text: Where there would be the cessation of the desired, the visible, and the seen —
Therefore the <s>Ātman</s> is of distinctive nature; it would itself become directly apparent (<s>aparokṣa</s>). [verse 1]

body.translated_text: Those who have ascertained the meaning through the knowledge of <s>Vedānta</s>, ascetics of purified nature through the yoga of renunciation (<s>saṃnyāsa</s>) — thus from the <s>śruti</s>. 'From the world up to the realm of <s>Brahmā</s>' — thus in the <s>Gītā</s>.

children.translated_text: As long as the <s>Ātman</s> is not known, the sage [gains only] a particle of the doer's attainment;
Until then, everything is futile, like a barren woman adorned. [verse 2]

body.text:
iti karmaparaḥ / parantu anarthakārī dehanāśakārī / tasmājjñānāya sādhayet /
tatra cakram ādhāraṃ nāma deham // 1 // svādhiṣṭhānaṃ sāttvikamahaṅkāraḥ // 2 // maṇipuraṃ buddhiḥ // 3 //
body.translated_text: Thus what pertains to <s>karma</s> (action). But in truth, it is the producer of harm and the destroyer of the body. Therefore one should strive for knowledge. Therein: the <s>cakra</s> called <s>Ādhāra</s> (support) means the body (1); <s>Svādhiṣṭhāna</s> means <s>sāttvika ahaṅkāra</s> (the pure ego) (2); <s>Maṇipura</s> means <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) (3);

body.text: anāhataṃ sadācāraḥ // 4 // viśuddhaṃ guhabhaktiḥ // 5 // ājñācakre jñāne sāvadhānatā // 6 // sahasradalaṃ turyā // 7 // trikūṭaṃ guṇarahitam // 8 // śrīhaṭhaṃ māyārahitam // 9 //
body.translated_text: <s>Anāhata</s> means righteous conduct (<s>sadācāra</s>) (4); <s>Viśuddha</s> means devotion to the Guru (<s>gurubhakti</s>) (5); at the <s>Ājñā-cakra</s>, attentiveness to knowledge (6); <s>Sahasradala</s> (thousand-petaled) means the fourth state (<s>turīya</s>) (7); <s>Trikūṭa</s> means free from the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) (8); <s>Śrīhaṭha</s> means free from <s>māyā</s> (illusion) (9);

body.text: gohaṭhamavidyātiraskāraḥ // 10 // bhruvorgumphā kāmanāśūnyam // 11 // brahmarandhraṃ manolayaḥ // 12 // sūlabandhamindriyanigrahaḥ // 13 // yānaṃ viṣayanirāsaḥ // 14 // jālandharaṃ svapararahitam // 15 // ṭālī padārthavārtāśūnyam // 16 // lolī yuktāhāraḥ // 17 // dhotī sarvajale 'pyaikyam // 18 // lambikā stutinindārahitam // 19 // khecarī avakāśe dṛṣṭiḥ // 20 // bhūcarī yugmamātramavalokanam // 21 // mahākāṣṭhā sarvaṃ brahmeti niścayaḥ // 22 // udgānamaniketam // 23 // lopanaṃ kāryātītam // 24 // gāṭhanaṃ dehaduḥkhasahanam // 25 // avakāśama dehātītam // 26 // iḍāpiṅgalayornāma // 27 // 28 // prapañcabuddhirahitam //
body.translated_text: <s>Gohaṭha</s> means the dispelling of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) (10); the knot between the eyebrows (<s>bhrūvorgumphā</s>) means free from desire (11); <s>Brahmarandhra</s> means the dissolution of the mind (<s>manolaya</s>) (12); the trident-lock (<s>sūlabandha</s>) means control of the senses (<s>indriya-nigraha</s>) (13); the vehicle (<s>yāna</s>) means the rejection of sense objects (14); <s>Jālandhara</s> means free from self and other (15); <s>Ṭālī</s> means empty of talk about objects (16); <s>Lolī</s> means regulated diet (<s>yuktāhāra</s>) (17); <s>Dhotī</s> means oneness with all waters (18); <s>Lambikā</s> means free from praise and blame (19); <s>Khecarī</s> means vision in space (20); <s>Bhūcarī</s> means seeing only the pair [of dualities] (21); <s>Mahākāṣṭhā</s> means the conviction 'all is <s>Brahman</s>' (22); <s>Udgāna</s> means homeless (<s>aniketa</s>) (23); <s>Lopana</s> means beyond action (24); <s>Gāṭhana</s> means enduring bodily suffering (25); <s>Avakāśa</s> means transcending the body (26); <s>Iḍā</s> and <s>Piṅgalā</s> by name (27, 28) mean free from worldly cognition.

children.translated_text: Thus the wise one should practice — not through bodily deception;
The <s>Ātman</s> is of distinctive nature from the body — in vain do people wander.

body.text: iti pātañjalahaṭhayogaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Pātañjala</s>-<s>Haṭha Yoga</s>.

children.translated_text: Now, the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>-<s>Rāja Yoga</s>:
Without <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, direct perception does not arise for the <s>Ātma-yogins</s>;
The body is to be abandoned like a sheath (<s>kañcuka</s>); one's own [Self] shines like space. [verse 1]

children.text: yaṃ śaivāḥ samupāsate śiva iti brahmeti vedāntino
children.translated_text: What the <s>Śaivas</s> worship as <s>Śiva</s>, what the <s>Vedāntins</s> call <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: bauddhā buddha iti pramāṇapaṭavaḥ karteti naiyāyikāḥ /
children.translated_text: What the <s>Buddhists</s> [know as] <s>Buddha</s>, what those skilled in logic (<s>Naiyāyikas</s>) [call] the Maker (<s>Kartṛ</s>),
What the followers of <s>Jaina</s> teaching [call] <s>Arhat</s>, what the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> [call] <s>karma</s> (action) —
All are whirling about, deficient in [understanding] the manifest world — there is nothing other than <s>Sāṃkhya</s>. [verse 2]
One should practice <s>Sāṃkhya Yoga</s> — <s>Puruṣa</s> is the twenty-fifth [principle];
Thus the <s>śruti</s>, the Vedic statement, is spoken by the good <s>Vedāntins</s>. [verse 3]
<s>Sāṃkhya</s> is the filling of space (<s>ākāśa</s>); <s>yoga</s> is the filling of air (<s>samīra</s>);
The <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is distinct from the body — therefore one should practice <s>Sāṃkhya</s>.
Dissolution is the cessation of all its expressions — the separateness of the <s>Ātman</s>;

children.text: sa sāṃkhyayogasaṃjñā ca itaraṃ bhrāmikaṃ matam // 5 //
children.translated_text: That is called <s>Sāṃkhya-yoga</s>; anything else is considered erroneous.
The <s>Ātman</s> is indeed distinct from everything — the one [appears as] many forms;

children.text: ekamevādvitīyaṃ brahma alaṃ tataḥ paraṃ bhavet (?) // 6 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> is one only, without a second — enough, nothing further exists beyond that.

body.text: iti sāṃkhyayogaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus <s>Sāṃkhya-yoga</s>.

children.translated_text: Now, the characteristics of the body:
Enjoyment, disease, impurity, death, and migration through bodily forms —
These follow <s>prārabdha</s> (destiny already set in motion) — such is indeed established.
The five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) and [gross] elements, the entire perceptible world —
<s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), and actions function through the light of consciousness.
When the mind rises within the body, that action is called <s>jīva</s> (individual soul);
When the mind rises through the body, that action is called body-bound.
The relation of food and eater — element is joined with element;
For that purpose, hear from me, dear child, the five elements in order.

children.text: āpaḥ pṛthivī bhakṣyaṃ ca vāyuragniśca bhakṣakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Water and earth are the food; wind and fire are the eaters;
Therein, space is the container; existence is designated as pure consciousness alone.
Hunger, thirst, and excretion — these are merely the actions of the body;
Other necessary actions are ordained as <s>Veda</s> (knowledge/scripture).
Steadfastness and equanimity, [being] an all-consumer yet without craving —
The undivided five elements — by these characteristics the body is described.

body.text: tatrāhamantaḥkaraṇaṃ bhoktā, bhoktā nāma sākṣitvam indriyāṇāṃ bhogasādhanatā nāma rasaparīkṣā pañcabhūtānāṃ bhogyaṃ nāma sthūlakṛśādidravyaguṇāḥ / yathā bhavanti tathā / tatra pramāṇaṃ śrutiḥ- tābhyaḥ puruṣamānayattā abruvanpuruṣaṃ stuteti puruṣo vā vasu kṛtaṃ yathāyatanaṃ praviśāmi kṣutpipāse bhavateti śruteḥ mātābālakanyāyena tatra gītāsu

children.translated_text: This body, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, is called the field (<s>kṣetra</s>);

children.text: etadyo vetti tama prāhuḥ kṣetrajña iti tadvidaḥ // 8 //
children.translated_text: One who knows this — the knowers of that call him the knower of the field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>).

body.translated_text: Therein, the 'I' is the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> (inner instrument), the experiencer. The experiencer means the witness-nature of the senses. The instrumentality for experience means the discernment of the essences of the five elements. The object of experience means the qualities of substances such as gross and subtle. They exist as they are. The authority therein is the <s>śruti</s>: 'From them they brought <s>Puruṣa</s>; they said to <s>Puruṣa</s>: "Praise!" <s>Puruṣa</s> indeed is the treasure created [by the gods]; "I shall enter each abode; let hunger and thirst be."' From this <s>śruti</s>, by the analogy of the mother and child, there [we find] in the <s>Gītā</s>:

body.text: iti sāṃkhyaparibhāṣā (1) //
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Sāṃkhyaparibhāṣā</s> (1).

children.text: (1) sāṃkhyaparibhāṣāgranthasya ekamevādarśapustakaṃ prāptamapi ca granthakṛtā granthaprārambhe-
children.translated_text: (1) Only one manuscript copy of the <s>Sāṃkhyaparibhāṣā</s> text was obtained. Moreover, the author of the text states at the beginning of the work:

children.text: vibhaktimatra yo paśyettasya jñānaṃ ca dūrataḥ /
children.translated_text: One who sees division here — knowledge is far from him.
By the grace of the <s>Guru</s>'s method, one gains insight into the womb of the scripture.

body.text: iti pratijñātatvādasya mudraṇe kārite bahuṣu sthaleṣu agatyā 'śuddhirasti kintu granthārtharakṣārthaṃ na tannirāse 'smābhirdṛṣṭipātaḥ kṛtaḥ / grantho 'pi khaṇḍita ivābhāti /
body.translated_text: Since this was pledged [by the author], in having this printed, there are unavoidably many impurities in numerous places; however, for the sake of preserving the meaning of the text, we have not cast our gaze upon their removal. The text also appears to be fragmentary.
